full_judgment:
Nozrul Islam Chowdhury J: This Reference under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been made by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 7 of 1999 for confirmation of death sentences imposed upon the condemned prisoners (1) Resalder Moslemuddin alias Moslemuddin (Retd) alias Hiron Khan alias Muslemuddin (2) Dafadar Marfot Ali Shah (3) LD (Dafadar) Md Abul Hashem Mridha, by his judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 20-10-2004.

2. By the self-same judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 20-10-2004 the Metropolitan Sessions Judge has also convicted 12 other accused persons under sections 302/109 of the Penal Code sentencing each of them thereunder to suffer imprisonment for life with fine of Tk. 10,000 each, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6 (six) months more.

3. Out of the aforesaid 12 accused persons sentenced to imprisonment for life 5 of them have preferred 4 appeals which are as under.

4. Lieutenant Colonel Syed Farook Rahman (Released) preferred Criminal Appeal No. 4739 of 2004 and Syed Mizanur Rahman, Advocate appears on his behalf. Lieutenant Colonel Sultan Shahriar Rashid Khan, EB (Released) preferred Criminal Appeal No. 4740 of 2004 and he is being represented by his learned Advocate Mr Abdur Razak Khan, Major (Retd) Bazlul Huda has preferred Jail Appeal No. 118 of 2006 and on his behalf Mr Abdullah-al-Mamun, the learned Advocate appears with the same while Major (Retd) AKM Mohiuddin Ahmed has preferred Jail Appeal No. 597 of 2007 and he is also being represented by Mr Abdullah-al- Mamun.

5. The aforesaid Reference and the appeals having arisen out of the self-same judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 20-10-2004 passed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge Mr Alhaj Md Motiur Rahman in Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 7 of 1999, all the aforesaid proceedings are being disposed of by the self-same judgment. Since all of those have already been heard by us analogously.

6. The prosecution case, in short, is that on November, 3, 1975 at about dawn Inspector General of Prisons Nuruzzaman Howlader brought Mr Kazi Abdul Awal, DIG (Prisons) to the Jail Gate by sending his Car for the purpose. Upon arrival at the Jail Gate Kazi Abdul Awal took his seat at the office of the IG (Prisons) at the Jail Gate and while sitting IG (Prisons) received various telephone calls; some time thereafter Captain Muslemuddin along with 4 other armed personnel had arrived at the Jail Gate but they did not disclose their names to the persons attending the Jail Gate but the informant PW 1 Kazi Abdul Awal ordered them to put their respective signatures in the register maintained for the purpose at the Jail Gate, before they could be allowed to enter into the Jail; thereafter putting their signatures they having entered into the Jail the said armed personnel wanted to know who Mr Nuruzzaman was, then Mr Nuruzzaman the IG (Prisons) disclosed his identity; thereafter the armed personnel inquired as to whether they had kept aside those persons who were asked to be kept segregated, whereupon Mr Nuruzzaman, the IG (Prison) answered that he would do the same immediately, thereafter Mr Nuruzzaman wanted to know the purpose of such segregation of those inmates of the Jail, on such query those armed personnel disclosed that they would be done to death; hearing such reply Mr Nuruzzaman (PW 3) then wanted to have a telephonic call to the President of the Republic then he made a telephonic call to the President; thereafter the Jailor also received a telephone call from President Mostaque who also desired to have a talk to Mr Nuruzzaman, the IG (Prison) and ultimately talk took place between the President and IG (Prisons). Thereafter the DIG (Prisons) wanted to know as to what sort of instructions he received from the President in reply Nuruzzaman disclosed that Presi- dent ordered him to allow the 5 army personnel to do whatever they wanted. Thereafter the second gate inside the Jail was also opened and the informant had also followed those 4 army personnel along with Mr Nuruzzaman all of whom entered inside the Jail, crossing the second gate thereof, having entered inside the Jail those 5 armed personnel inquired as to why there was delay, in reply the informant disclosed that he also wanted to have a talk to the President but he was not allowed to do so. Then the informant wanted to go back but the IG (Prisons) did not allow him to do so; immediately thereafter the Deputy Jailor, Habilder and some wardens had informed that those persons have been segregated in the meantime, accordingly Muslemuddin and his 4 other armed companions had gone to the spot where the 4 Leaders namely (1) Syed Nazrul Islam (2) Captain Mansur Ali (3) Tajuddin Ahmed and (4) ARM Kamruzzaman were brought, as ordered and a few minutes thereafter the informant and others heard sounds of opening shots from the firearms; some time thereafter the assailants had decamped from the scene in a hurry. Thereafter the informant returned back to his office where he said his Fazor prayer and subsequently the informant came to know that another group of people had arrived at the scene of occurrence to ensure the death of those 4 leaders, thereafter informant gathered that out of the said 4 leaders 2 were alive but they have been done to death by bayonet charges by the 2nd group; the informant along with IG (Prisons) were at a fix, knowing not what to do at that time therefore left the office for their respective residence; they again returned back at 8-00/9-00 AM to the Jail Gate and the informant requested the IG (Prisons) to make contact with the army officials to know the course of action at that situation; in reply IG (Prisons) gave a telephone number over which the informant had a talk with Major Rashid who ordered not to move the dead bodies; at around mid-day on the same day the informant along with the IG (Prisons) had gone to the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs; they apprised him about the incident but he also failed to give any satisfactory solution rather he asked to hand over the dead bodies to their respective relations after concluding post mortem examinations over the same; at the same time the Secretary also had telephonic calls with Superintendent of Police, Deputy Commissioner, Civil Surgeon and others over the incident; the persons who had been killed by the said army personnel were Syed Nazrul Islam, Captain Mansur Ali, Mr Tajuddin Ahmed and Mr AHM Kamruzzaman and after handing over the dead bodies as instructed above, the informant lodged the first information report with the police station; thereafter the well-wishers of the informant requested him to withdraw the case but he refused to do so. The informant lodged the first information report on 4-11-1975 with Lalbagh Police Station with copy to different places keeping one copy at the Central Jail; thereafter on 5-11-1975 the informant also submitted a detailed report about the incident addressing the Inspector General of Prisons.

7 .The Investigating Officer investigated into the case who having visited the place of occurrence, prepared sketch map with index over the scene of occurrence, recorded statements of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and upon conclusion of the investigation submitted charge sheet No. 370 dated 15-10-1998 against 21 accused persons in GR Case No.1 0698 of 1975 under sections 120B/448/449/302/109/34 of the Penal Code.

8. It may not to be out of context to mention that on the basis of the first information report date 4-11-1975 lodged by PW 1 Kazi Abdul Awal the informant, Lalbagh PS Case No.11 dated 4-11-75 was registered, but the investigation was suspended for years together, presumably for political change.

9. Eventually the case was sent to the Court of Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka where it was registered as Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 7 of 1999.

10. Mr Md Motiur Rahman, the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, having taken up the case for trial framed charge under section 120B of the Penal Code against 20 accused persons. Since one of them named Aziz Pasha died in the meantime, charge was also framed against 19 accused persons under sections 302/109 of the Penal Code except Resalder Moslemuddin while Resalder Moslemuddin had separately been charged under section 302 of the Penal Code.

11: The prosecution examined as many as 64 witnesses in support of their case while the defence adduced none and upon conclusion of the trial the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge by his judgment and order dated 20-10-2004 convicted 3 accused persons under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code imposing capital punishment upon them who are Resalder Moslemuddin alias Moslemuddin (Retd) alias Hiron Khan alias Moslemuddin, Dafader Morfath Ali Shah and LD (Dafader) Md Abul Hashem Mridha (dismissed).

12. The aforesaid 3 convicts along with 12 others have also been convicted under sections 302/ 109 of the Penal Code sentencing each of them thereunder to suffer imprisonment for life with fine of Tk. 10,000 each, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6 (six) months.

13. All the accused persons have been acquitted from the charge under section 120B of the Penal Code by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, by his judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 20-10-2004 in Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 7 of 1999.

14. The aforesaid judgment and order of conviction and sentence has been challenged by the convicts in the aforesaid two regular appeals and two Jail appeals as detailed above while the Death Reference for confirmation of the sentence of death imposed upon three of them have been registered as Death Reference No.150 of 2004.

15. Mr Mansur Habib, the learned Additional Attorney-General appearing in support of the Reference, submits that Mr ASM Abdul Mobin, the learned Assistant Attorney-General, will make submissions on his behalf, therefore, we have allowed Mr Mobin to make his submission in support of the reference.

16. It may not be out of context to mention that initially, on behalf of the State Ms Sarker Tahmina Begum the learned Assistant Attorney-General having appeared before this Court on several days, has placed before us 2500 pages of Paper Books including the impugned judgment.

17. Mr ASM Abdul Mubin the learned Assistant Attorney-General at the out set submits that in the instant case the place of occurrence and time of occurrence has not been challenged by the defence. With reference to the first information report, he has pointed out that Exhibit 1 and 3 are the first information report in this case although the original first information report has unfortunately been lost in the case. Referring to the defects as noted in respect of first information report Mr Mobin placed reliance in the case of Somappa vs State of Mysore reported in AIR 1979 (SC) 1831 (1836 para 12) wherefrom he submits that even rejection of the first information report would not detract the testimonies of the eye-witnesses which can be assessed independently. Mr Mobin submits further that the first information report has got a presumption about the correctness in its favour under section 114( e) of the Evidence Act, therefore whatever defect as pointed out over the same it is incumbent upon the defence to rebut the presumption as contemplated under section 114( e) of the Evidence At. In support of his contention he then placed reliance in the case of Sonilal vs State of Uttar Prodesh reported in AIR 1978 (SC) 1142 (1143 para 11).

18. At that stage Mr Anisul Huq, the learned Senior Advocate appeared before this Court and has produced a Memo bearing No. 25/Solicitor/2004 (Part-1)-112 dated 30-7-2008 issued from the Solicitor Wing of Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs wherefrom it appears that he along with 6 other learned Advocates have been appointed in this case in addition to the Counsels for the State, therefore, we allowed Mr Anisul Huq to appear before us in support of the reference who having appeared before us pointed out that PWs 1,2, 3,5,6, 7, 8, 9 and 12 are the witnesses for the place of occurrence while PWs 11, 13, 16, 17, 18, 21 and 34 are the witnesses for the Bangabhaban part of the prosecution case that is for abetment while PWs 10, 19,20 are the inmates and prisoners of Jail which is the place of occurrence. Mr Huq has pointed out that from the part of the conspiracy as disclosed by the prosecution witnesses PWs 15, 27, 30, 35 and 38 appeared in support thereof while PWs 24, 25, 26, 32, 33 and 63 are formal witnesses. Mr Huq in support of his submission to the effect that the act of abetment has rightly been established in this case in respect of all the accused persons as supported by PWs 11,13, 16, 17, 18, 21 and 34. Substantiating his submission the learned Counsel refers to the provision of section 107 of the Penal Code specially to the Explanation thereof. At one stage in presence of Mr Anisul Huq, Mr Mobin pointed out certain circumstances in support of the reference as available in the instant case, for the purpose of confirmation thereof and those are (a) that the accused persons had been sitting at Bangabhaban as disclosed by PWs 11, 13, 16, 17, 18, 21 and 34 (b) Major Shariful Hoque Dalim visited the Jail prior to the time of occurrence on the same day as disclosed by PW s 19, 20 and 21 (c) information collected by Major Abdur Rashid and others as disclosed by PWs 2 and 3 (d) telephonic conversation in between Bangabhaban and the Jail Gate as disclosed by PWs 1, 2 and 3.

19. Mr Mobin submits further that, to bring home a charge of abetment no overt act is necessary and in support of such contention he has placed reliance in the case of Abdul Awal vs State, reported in 1994 BLD (AD) 224, and in the case of Baby John vs State reported in 1953 Criminal Law Journal 1273 (para 3) and also in the case of G. Anantha-chari vs State of Madras reported in 40 Criminal Law Journal 302(303). It is also submitted by Mr Mobin that on a charge of abetment upon the accused he may be convicted under section 34 of the Penal Code without altering the charge. In support of such contention the learned Assistant Attorney- General placed his reliance in the case of S Satta-narayan vs Emperor reported in 45 Criminal Law Journal 624 (630), and Emperor vs Javantilal Ravji reported in 48 Criminal Law Journal 419(422) and lastly, for the purpose of explanation available under section 34 of the Penal Code, the learned Assistant Attorney-General has referred to the case of King Emperor vs Barendra Kumar Gose 28 CWN 170 (244).

20. Pointing out certain discrepancies as detected by the trial Court Mr Mobin submits that discrepancies always occur even in the evidence of truthful witness and in support of such contention made by him the learned Assistant Attorney-General placed reliance in the case of Ataur Rahman vs State 43 DLR 87.

21. It is also contended by Mr Mobin that one part of the evidence even if rejected the other part of the same witness may be accepted in any case and to fortify such submission made by him, placed reliance in the case of Bazlu Talukder vs State 48 DLR 509.

22. Mr Md Hannan, the learned Advocate appearing as State Defence Lawyer on behalf of the absconding condemned prisoners, submits that the complicity of 2 out of 3 condemned prisoners i.e. Dafader Marfat Ali Shah, Ld (Dafader Abul Hashem Mridha could not be proved by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt, in that PW 1 Kazi Abdul Awal deposed to the effect that all the 5 army personnel put their signatures in the register at the Jail Gate before they had entered inside the Jail. Despite specific suggestion put to this witness (PW1) in this regard the prosecution did not produce the said register before the Court to prove the complicity of these .two convicts rather the said register has been deliberately withheld by the prosecution warranting adverse presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act against the prosecution case. Mr Hannan submits further that the so-called first information report was registered 36 hours after the occurrence yet the same contains only one name i.e Moslemuddin but the other two were not even named in the said first information report It is also submitted by Mr Hannan that Exhibit 2 is said to be a detailed report submitted by PW I DIG (Prisons) addressing the Inspector General of Prisons on 5-11-1975 but the said detailed report too, does not disclose the name of the said two condemned prisoners. It is also submitted by him that PWs 11, 13, 16, 17, 18 and 21 do not disclose the complicity of Dafader Marfat Ali Shah, Ld. (Dafader) Abul Hashem Mridha.

23. Pointing out the deposition of PW 21, Mr Hannan submits that as per the deposition of PW 21 Commodore Gholam Rabbani all the three condemned prisoners had been engaged as Guard of the President, as such, they were not supposed to go out of Bangabhaban as claimed by the prosecution. Lastly, Mr Hannan submits that it is about 21 years after the occurrence that names of the said two condemned prisoners were disclosed by the witnesses before the Investigating Officer for the first time and there was no disclosure about their complicity at any stage prior to such time, therefore, Mr Hannan submits that the complicity of these two condemned prisoners namely Dafader Marfat Ali Shah and Ld. (Dafader) Abul Hashem Mridha could not be proved beyond reasonable doubt. Lastly Mr Hannan has pointed out that in view of the prosecution case to the effect that it is the defence personnel who participated in the occurrence the case ought to have been tried under Court Martial under the Army Act, 1952 and the whole trial in the instant case has been vitiated as being without jurisdiction.

24. Mr Abdullah-al-Mamun, the learned Advocate appearing in two Jail Appeals being Jail Appeal No. 118 of 2008 brought by Major Bazlul Huda and Jail Appeal No. 597 of 2007 brought by Major AKM Mohiuddin Ahmed submits that regard being had to the acquittal of all the accused from the charge under section 120B of the Penal Code their conviction under sections 302/109 is not sustainable in law."

25. Mr Mamun submits further that the trial Court at the first part of the impugned judgment having discarded the testimonies of the material witnesses, erred in law in convicting the appellants relying on the testimonies of the same witnesses at the latter• part of the same judgment which, according to him, is not at all sustainable in law.

26. Elaborating his contention Mr Mamun submits further that the credibility of the same witnesses having been discarded once, cannot be relied upon subsequently in the same case.

27. Pointing out the contradictions and omission in material particulars by the witnesses the learned Counsel submits that those witnesses cannot at all be relied upon and the conviction based on the testimonies of those witnesses is not sustainable in law.

28. Mr Mamun submits further that the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside in view of self contradictions by learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge himself; in this connection he has referred to certain observations made by the learned Sessions Judge in the impugned judgment.

29. Referring to the Exhibits 1 and 3, the learned Counsel submits that those under no stretch of imagination can be treated as first information report in this case, in that the learned Advocate having referred to section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, submits further that neither Exhibit 1 nor Exhibit 3 contains the signatures of the informant nor any signature of the police officer who is alleged to have recorded the same is available therein although such a signature is the essential ingredient in an first information report as contemplated under section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In this connection, the learned Advocate has referred to the depositions of PW 1 who deposed to the effect that :

“ ১৯৭৫ সনে ঢাকা কেন্দ্রীয় কারাগারে কোন ফটোস্টেট মেশিন ছিল না তাহা সত্য। এজাহারে যে ফটোকপি আদালতে দাখিল করা হইয়াছে এবং যাহা প্রদর্শনী হিসাবে চিহ্নিত করা হইয়াছে তাহাতে আমার কোন স্বাক্ষর নাই তাহা সত্য।”

30. It is also pointed out by the learned Counsel that PW 1 has admitted in his cross examination to the effect that:

“আমার কাছ হইতে যে এজাহারের কপি নেওয়া হয় তাহাতে দুই স্বাক্ষীর স্বাক্ষর আছে তাহা সত্য।”

31. Pointing out the deposition of PW 64 the investigating officer of this case to the effect that:

“ আই, জি অফিস হইতে এজাহারের অবিকল নকল প্রাপ্ত হইয়া আদালতে প্রঃ ৩ দাখিল করি। ঢাকা কেন্দ্রীয় কারাগারে বাদী আবদুল আউয়ালের সহিত করা একটি এজাহার প্রাপ্ত হই। উহা জব্দ তালিকার মাধ্যমে জব্দ করি। এই সেই টাইপ করা এজাহার প্রঃ-১।”

32. In this connection the learned Counsel submits further that PW 1 admitted in his cross- examination that Exhibit 1 does not contain his signature. Pointing out the aforesaid anomalies the learned Advocate submits that the instant case having been based on inherent infirmities the conviction against the appellants is not sustainable in law.

33. Referring to the depositions of PW 29 Colonel Shafayet Zamil to the effect that:

“২রা নভেম্বর/৭৫ এর রাত্র ১২.০০/১.০০টার সময় পরিকল্পনা মাফিক ২ infantry কোম্পানী ক্যান্টনমেন্টে ফিরিয়া আসে। company দুইটির কমান্ডার ছিলেন মেজর ইকবাল এবং মেজর মাহমুদুর রহমান। Chief of Staff জেনারেল জিয়া বঙ্গবভনে অবস্থায়রত বিদ্রোহীদের কাছ থেকে বিছিন্ন করার জন্য ক্যাপটেইন হাফিজুল্লার নেতৃত্বে একজন সেনা পাঠানো হয়। ক্যাপটেইন হাফিজুল্লা টেলিফোন যোগাযোগ বিচ্ছিন্ন করে রাখে। যাহাতে খন্দকার মুশতাক বিদ্রোহী অফিসারেরা যোগযোগ রাখতে অসমর্থ হয়। ২রা নভেম্বর/৭৫ এর রাত্র ১২.০০/১.০০টার পর troops withdraw সহ পরবর্তী আমাদের কর্মকান্ড troops deply সহ ক্যান্টনম্যান্ট হইতে সমস্ত কিছু পরিচালনা করা হয়। আবার ৩ তারিখ সকাল ভোর হইতে troops deployment শুরু হয়।”

34. Mr Mamun submits that at around the time of occurrence all the accused persons had been confined inside the Bangabhaban and it was not at all possible on their part to get out of the same far less taking part in commission of the crime as alleged against them.

35. Mr Mamun submit lastly that in the instant case the statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in respect of the witnesses were recorded some time in the year 1996 i.e about 22 years after the occurrence and because of the belated recording of the statements in respect of the witnesses, testimonies of those witnesses have been rendered doubtful.

36. To substantiate his submission to the effect discrepancies, material omission and the contradiction in the statement of the witnesses, particularly of the eye-witnesses, render their testimonies doubtful. Mr Mamun placed reliance in the case of Nurul Islam vs State reported in 1994 BLD (AD) 69 = 43 DLR (AD) 6.

37. In substantiating his submission to the effect that a conviction under section 109 of the Penal Code it is necessary that there must be some evidence of overt act or omission so as to suggest a preconcert or common design to commit a particular offence. The learned Counsel refers to the case of Ali Ahmed Malaker alias Kunai alias Malaker vs State reported in 43 DLR 401. He also relied on the decision in the case of Murad Ali vs State reported in 22 DLR (WP) 158 on the same point.

38. It is also submitted that for the purpose of maintaining a conviction for the offence of abetment the identity of the accused must have been established and in the absence of such identity charge of abetment fails.

39. To substantiate such submission the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case of State vs Mokbul Hussain reported in 26 DLR 419.

40. On the point of belated examination of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which renders the testimonies of the witnesses doubtful, the learned Counsel for the appellants placed reliance in the case of State vs Monu Meah, reported in 6 BLC 402, and in the case of Moinullah vs State reported in 40 DLR 443 and also the case of Babu Mollah vs State reported in 4 BLC 559.

41. Mr Abdur Rezzak Khan, the learned Counsel appears on behalf of Lieutenant Colonel Sultan Shahriar Rashid Khan in Criminal Appeal No. 4740 of 2004 and submits that in the instant case the prosecution failed to produce any evidence on record against the appellant Sultan Shahriar Rashid Khan that he had ever taken a decision for sending the assailants to the Jailor he had ever participated in the telephonic conversation between the Bangabhaban and the Jail as alleged by the prosecution or for that matter he had participated in any act facilitating entry of the assailants into the Jail therefore, his conviction under sections 302/109 is not sustainable in law.

42. Mr Khan submits further that the charge as framed does not disclose the factum of going out or coming into Bangabhaban by the appellant therefore any inference on the basis of going out or coming in is not sustainable in law.

43. Mr Khan has referred to the findings and observations of the trial Court as available in the earlier part of the same judgment which directly contradicts the findings available on the latter part of the self-same judgment, therefore, Mr Khan submits that the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is not at all sustainable in law in that it is a self-contradictory one. Referring to the circumstantial evidence as pointed out by the learned Counsel Mr Khan submits that there being missing-links in between the chain of circumstances disclosed by the witnesses the conviction on the basis of circumstantial evidence is also not sustainable.

44. To substantiate his submission the learned Counsel refers to the case of Osman Gani vs State reported in 55 DLR (AD) 34 and the case of State vs Arman Ali reported in 42 DLR (AD) 50 on the point of belated disclosure of the complicity of the appellant. The learned Counsel also placed reliance in the case of Nowabul Alam vs State reported in 1995 BLD (AD) 54 = 45 DLR (AD) 140 and in the case of Muslimuddin vs State reported in 1987 BLD (AD) 1 = 38 DLR (AD) 311.

45. Mr Syed Mizanur Rahman, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of Lieutenant Colonel Syed Farook Rahman in Criminal Appeal No.4739 of 2004, submits with referable to the evidence on record that the telephone link with Bangabhaban was snapped at 12-00 midnight or 1-00 AM on August 2, 1975 because of coup d'etat declared by Brigadier Khaled Mosharaf, therefore it was neither possible for the appellant to take part in any telephonic conversation from Bangabhaban with the Jail authority nor there was any scope left for going out or coming in or in taking part in any offence as alleged by the prosecution.

46. Pointing out the cross-examination portion of the witnesses Mr Syed Mizanur Rahman submits that the duty register of Bangabhaban in respect of PWs 11, 13, 16, 17, 18 and 34 showing them as employees of Bangabhaban at the relevant time was deliberately withheld by the prosecution warranting adverse presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act.

47. Pointing out the admission of PWs  1 and 3 to the effect that on the fateful night security alarm was proclaimed inside the Jail and the BDR personnel were also called in for the security of the Jail on the same day yet there had been no resistance at all by the Jail authority to the perpetrators of the crime who had forced their way inside the Jail, there- fore, he submits that the occurrence did not take place in the manner as alleged by the prosecution.

48. In view of the submissions made by the learned Counsel appearing from both sides it is imperative to assess and evaluate the evidence on record for the purpose of assessment of correct position in the case.

49. We have already pointed out that 64 witnesses have been examined by the prosecution in this case and of them PW 1 Kazi Abdul Awal who had been serving as DIG of Prisons in the year 1975. This witness in his deposition disclosed to the effect that on November 3, 1975 at about dawn he was brought to Dhaka Central Jail Gate by the car sent by Inspector General of Prisons Mr Nuruzzaman Howlader and while he was sitting with the IG (Prisons) at his office at that time IG Prisons had received several telephonic calls. Some times thereafter Captain Moslemuddin along with 4 armed defence personnel had arrived at the Jail Gate who had refrained from disclosing their names but PW 1 having insisted upon, obtained their signatures in the register maintained in the Jail Gate for the purpose of entry inside the Jail. Those 5 army personnel inquired as to who Mr Nuruzzaman was, in reply Mr Nuruzzaman, IG (Prisons) disclosed his identity thereafter they wanted to know as to whether the named persons were segregated as was asked for, then Mr Nuruzzaman replied that he was taking steps for the same, at that point Mr Nuruzzaman wanted to know the reason for such segregation of those persons; answer was that they would be killed. Then Mr Nuruzzaman expressed his anxiety to talk to the President and then telephonic talk in between the IG (Prisons) and the President took place. After killing of Bangabandhu along with his relations on 15th August, 1975, Major Dalim, Major Rashid, Major Shahriar and Major Farook used to enquire about the political leaders detained in the Central Jail. They used to do so on behalf of President Khandaker Mostaque Ahmed from Bangabhaban. On the evening of November 2,1975 while he was working at his office at that time Major Dalim had gone to the Central Jail with arms and he wanted to go inside the Jail. PW 2 then asked him that he would inform the matter to the higher authority at which Major Dalim dished out threat and ordered him to take him in. PW 2 being aware of the authority of Major Dalim accompanied him inside the Jail out of fear. When Major Dalim wanted to see for himself the position of Awami League leaders there inside the Jail so PW 2 Jailor Aminur Rahman took Dalim to cell No.15 of New Jail where he moved around, thereafter he had also talk with former Police Super of Dhaka Mr Mahbubuddin who was then detained inside the Jail, subsequently he went out of the Jail. On the same day at night Major Farook wanted to know the position of Awami League leaders from Bangabhaban over telephone. At dead of night on November 3,1975 at about 3-00 AM the guard of the Jail on duty at the Jail Gate made a telephone call to PW 2 asking him to rush to the Jail Gate. Having stepped up security measures, PW 2 rushed to the Jail Gate at 3-00 AM then the guard on duty at the gate informed him that the Inspector General of Prisons had arrived at the gate so PW 2 received the JG (Prisons) and arranged for a sitting at the office of DIG (Prisons) who informed him that some time before, he had received a telephonic call whereby he was informed that some miscreants might kidnap some inmates of the Jail by force so he ordered to step up security measures for the purpose. He further informed PW 2 that DIG (Prisons) Kazi Abdul Awal was also supposed to reach the Jail Gate, meanwhile the DIG (Prisons) Abdul Awal rushed to the Jail Gate and had joined the Inspector General of Prisons, DIG (Prisons) while sitting at their office, on the instruction of Inspector General of Prisons, security alarm was proclaimed inside the Jail to get the security force alert; hearing the alarm DIG (Prisons), Deputy Jailor Abdul Zahid, Md Toyab Ali Mollah, Mohammad Abdur Rouf, Md Aman Ullah Md Iqbal Hossain had converged at the Jail Gate, they were also accompanied by Assistant Surgeon Dr Rafique Ahmed and 2 other doctors; at that moment Inspector General of Prisons received a telephone call from Bangabhaban whereby he was informed that an army man bearing the name Captain Moslemuddin along with some other army personnel would reach the Jail Gate and PW 2 was asked to receive them so that they may be brought to the office of the Deputy Inspector General of Prisons; at about 4-00 AM Captain Moslemuddin along with other 4 armed personnel had gone to the Jail Gate who were duly received by PW 2 and upon obtaining their signatures in the register kept in the gate, those 5 persons were taken to the office of the Deputy Inspector General of Prisons where Inspector General of Prisons was also present; then PW 2 returned back to his office room where he received a telephone from Major Rashid who wanted to talk to Inspector General of Prisons. This message was carried to Inspector General of Prisons whereupon he came and received the telephone call. Over the telephonic call Inspector General of Prisons had a talk with President Khandaker Mostaque Ahmed; having a talk over telephone with the President, Inspector General of Prisons informed PW 2 to the effect that he had been asked to act according to the desire of those 5 armed personnel; at that time Captain Moslemuddin desired to go inside the Jail whereupon Inspector General of Prisons accompanied them inside the Jail along with PW 2 and others. It was also deposed by PW 2 that Captain Moslemuddin along with those 4 army personnel were dressed with khaki and black uniforms but there were no badge on their shoulder; entering into the Jail Gate Captain Muslim wanted to go to the place where leaders of Awami League were detained so they were taken to the new Jail where the 4 leaders of the Awami League were detained at that time Captain Muslim directed for keeping the 4 leaders segregated in a particular room, which was however complied by PW 2 along with Sobedar Abdul Wahed Mridha and the Principal guard of the Jail along with other guards available and those leaders were confined to room No.1 of cell No.15 of the New Jail and the matter was informed to the army personnel whereupon they having entered into room No.1 of cell No.15 they had opened fire indiscriminately; pointing the 4 leaders whereby they were killed; thereafter the assailants decamped from the scene. PW 2 deposed further that he was bewildered at the horrific scene and all of them returned back to the Jail Gate, at that moment Azan for Fazor prayer was being proclaimed. PW 2 had started for going for prayer, at that moment gate keeper rushed to him and had informed that 4 other army personnel had again arrived at the gate so PW 2 rushed to the gate without saying his prayer. The gate keeper obtained their respective signatures in the gate register then one of the said 4 persons uttered “শ্যালা ভিতরে চল, নেতারা মরিয়াছে কিনা তাহা নিশ্চিত করিতে হইবে।”out of fear the guard opened the gate whereupon those 4 persons rushed inside the spot and had charged the victims with bayonets carried by them. Thereafter at 11-00 AM on 3-11-75 PW 2 along with Sobedar Abdul Awal Mridha had gone to the room No.1 of cell No.15 where they found the dead bodies of Syed Nazrul Islam, Tajuddin Ahmed, Captain Mansur Ali and Kamruzzaman were lying in a pool of blood and with the help of Chief guard the 4 dead bodies were arranged northwise (as generally done by Muslims after death). This witness also preserved the wrist watch and rings of Syed Nazrul Islam and Tajuddin Ahmed at his office, till 4-11-75 the dead bodies of the 4 leaders remained in the same room No.1 at the order of the highest authority without making any arrangement for shifting therefrom.
